rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (kd 0.9, kp 1.6, base_speed 1.1) is still the best raced design at 511.25. Its oval finished 20/20 at 2.00 s, with steering_oscillation 0.185. Its s-bend reached 5/20 finishes with mean max_error 0.0608 m, and its slalom ended off track 20/20 with max_error 0.066 m. Iteration 7 raised kd to 1.0 and scored 447.29, a clear drop. The s-bend fell to 1/20 finishes, and s-bend steering_oscillation rose to 0.236 on the one-run mean, with more bend losses. So kd has passed its useful range, and the Evaluator's rule to return kd to 0.9 applies. Over kd 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 the s-bend max_error stayed at 0.060 to 0.061 m, and speed (1.3, 1.1, 1.0) did not move it either. The remaining lever is proportional gain. Change: controller.kp from 1.6 to 1.4, with kd returned to 0.9 and everything else fixed (base_speed 1.1, ki 0, sensor_weights -2..2, last_direction, and the iteration 3 to 6 geometry: x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.05, sensor_size 0.012). Expected result: less steering overshoot on bends, so s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m and s-bend finishes rise above 5/20, with the oval staying at 20/20 near 2.0 s. Risk: at kp 1.4 the response may be too slow on the tighter slalom corners, and progress may drop. Hypotheses to check: (1) kp is now the limiting gain for bend overshoot; (2) the flat max_error across speed and kd points at the sensor layout, which may be limiting how early the robot sees a bend. Measurements wanted: per-track finish rate, max_error, steering_oscillation and completion_time, especially on the s-bend and slalom. If the oval drops below 20/20 or the slalom progress falls, return kp to 1.6 and try a sensor-geometry test next.
